Inter Account Transfer — Edit

The Inter Account Transfer form is used to transfer money between your bank accounts and cash accounts.

This form allows you to record movements of funds when you deposit cash into a bank account, withdraw cash from a bank account, or transfer money between different bank accounts.

When to Use Inter Account Transfers

Use an inter account transfer when moving money between accounts that you control. Common examples include:

• Depositing cash takings into your bank account

• Withdrawing cash from the bank for petty cash

• Transferring funds between your business bank accounts

• Moving money from your main account to a savings account

Important Notes

Inter account transfers do not affect your profit and loss statement, as they only move money between your own accounts.

If you need to record payments to suppliers or receipts from customers, use Payment or Receipt forms instead.

Form Fields

Complete the following fields to record your transfer:

Date

Enter the date of the transfer. This is when the money moves between accounts.

The transfer date affects bank reconciliations and cash flow reports.

Reference

Enter a reference number for this transfer. This could be a transaction number or description to identify the transfer.

References help match transfers with bank statements and provide an audit trail.

Description

Optionally, add a description or notes about this transfer, such as the purpose or reason for moving funds.

Common reasons include funding petty cash, moving funds for payroll, or consolidating accounts.

Paid from

Select the bank or cash account from which money is being transferred out.

This account's balance will be reduced by the transfer amount.

CreditAmount

Enter the amount being transferred out of the source account. This will be credited (reduced) from the 'Paid from' account.

For transfers between accounts with the same currency, this amount equals what is received.

CreditClearStatus

For bank accounts, select whether this withdrawal has cleared the bank or is still pending.

Pending transactions appear in bank reconciliations as uncleared items.

Received in

Select the bank or cash account into which money is being transferred.

This account's balance will be increased by the transfer amount.

DebitAmount

If transferring between accounts with different currencies, enter the amount received in the destination account's currency.

The difference between amounts sent and received represents the exchange gain or loss.

DebitClearStatus

For bank accounts, select whether this deposit has cleared the bank or is still pending.

Deposits may clear on a different date than withdrawals, especially for inter-bank transfers.

Exchange rate

When transferring between accounts with different currencies, enter the exchange rate used for the conversion.

Use the actual rate from your bank or the rate at which you exchanged the currencies.
